questions.question: Which type best describes the body of a PATCH endpoint that may update any field of `Loan` except `id`?
questions.explanation: Omit removes id, and Partial makes every remaining property optional, so the client can send any subset of the editable fields.

questions.question: Given `const p: Readonly<{ name: string; address: { city: string } }>`, which assignment compiles?
questions.explanation: Readonly is shallow: it marks only top-level properties readonly. The nested address object is still mutable, so p.address.city can be reassigned.

questions.question: For `async function fetchLoan(): Promise<Loan>` (or one inferred to return a promise of Loan), which type gives you `Loan`?
questions.explanation: ReturnType gives Promise<Loan>; Awaited unwraps the promise to Loan. typeof is required because fetchLoan is a value, not a type.

questions.question: What is the difference between `Omit` and `Exclude`?
options: They are aliases for the same type
Omit works on union members; Exclude works on object keys
Omit removes keys from an object type; Exclude removes members from a union type
Exclude only works with string literals; Omit works with any type
questions.explanation: Omit<T, K> produces an object type without the keys K. Exclude<U, X> filters a union, keeping members not assignable to X, for example Exclude<Method, "CASH">.
